purpose: Anchor A7 (ESP32) antenna delay calibration, against T1 held FIXED at 16428.
note_on_distance: User corrected the distance mid-calibration from an initially given 4184mm to 6585mm. All measurements below used 6585mm.
anomaly: This board's measured range drifted monotonically upward across the whole calibration session regardless of the correction applied (raw sequence: 6530.78 -> 6619.45 -> 6639.52mm), making two consecutive corrections appear to move the residual in the WRONG direction (a correction that should have reduced the residual instead coincided with it growing). Ruled out a config-application bug first: confirmed RANGE,START calls radio_reconfigure(cfg()) via the same platform-agnostic core/serial.c path already proven correct on A1-A6, so the antenna-delay writes were taking effect. Characterized the drift with two back-to-back 60s NO-CHANGE windows (residuals 76.2mm, 84.8mm -- consistent with each other, and their sub-chunk deltas were much smaller than the earlier change-driven jumps), then a 90s post-correction window whose six sub-chunks were flat (6592-6611mm, no trend) -- confirming the drift had settled, most likely thermal warm-up specific to this board (the only ESP32 anchor, freshly connected for this calibration).

passes.note: residual grew instead of shrinking -- first sign of the drift, not yet recognized as such
residual grew AGAIN in the same direction after a correctly-signed correction -- stopped reactive correcting here and diagnosed instead
windows agree closely with each other (8.5mm apart); combined mean used for the next correction rather than any single noisy pass
six sub-chunks over 90s show NO trend -- drift has settled

lesson: Before reacting to an unexpected-direction residual with another correction, check for drift with a no-change window pair first -- a superimposed drift trend can make a correctly-signed correction look backwards. This cost 3 wasted correction passes before being caught.
